title: 东北硬菜①锅包肉：这道菜，居然是为外国人发明的 | Northeast Comfort Food P1 · Guobaorou 🍖
description:
锅包肉，你是番茄汁派，还是老式糖醋派？ / Guobaorou: are you team ketchup, or team old-school vinegar?

第①集·锅包肉 —— 「东北硬菜」系列，每天一道东北招牌菜。
P1 · Guobaorou — from the series Northeast Comfort Food: one Dongbei classic a day.

这道东北菜的「扛把子」，居然是为外国人发明的。1907年，郑兴文进哈尔滨滨江关道衙门（道台府）当官厨，专给道台与外宾料理膳食。外国客人吃不惯北方的咸鲜口味，郑兴文就把咸鲜的「焦炒肉片」改成酸甜口味，外壳酥脆、酸甜挂汁——哈尔滨从此成了锅包肉的起源地。它本叫「锅爆肉」，因为洋人点菜发音，日子久了衍化成今天的「锅包肉」。到了今天，它分成两大流派：透亮的老式糖醋，和偏甜的番茄汁——一道菜，两派吵了快一百年。
The heavyweight of Dongbei cooking was actually invented for foreigners. In 1907, chef Zheng Xingwen joined the official's kitchen in Harbin, cooking for the magistrate and his foreign guests. The guests couldn't take the savory northern flavor, so Zheng reworked a salty fried-pork dish into a crisp, sweet-and-sour one — making Harbin the birthplace of guobaorou. Originally named guo-bao-rou (“wok-blasted pork”), the name drifted through foreign diners' pronunciation into what we call it today. Now it splits two ways: the clear old-school vinegar style, and the sweeter ketchup style — one dish, two camps, a near-century-long feud.
